locations.name: The New York Public Library
locations.factShort: It stands on the drained bed of the Croton Reservoir, whose Egyptian-style walls held the city's water supply until 1900. The lions were named Patience and Fortitude by La Guardia during the Depression, for the qualities he thought New Yorkers needed.

locations.name: Kings Theatre
locations.factShort: A 1929 Loew's Wonder Theatre that sat derelict for thirty-eight years with rain coming through the roof onto its plasterwork. A ninety-five million dollar restoration reopened it in 2015, matching the original French Baroque interior from photographs.

locations.name: The Steinway & Sons Factory
locations.factShort: Steinway built not just a factory here but a company town with housing, a school and a fire station, on farmland far from Manhattan's labour unrest. Each concert grand still takes about a year to build, much of it by hand.

locations.name: The Grand Concourse
locations.factShort: Modelled on the Champs-Élysées and opened in 1909, its four-and-a-half miles hold one of the largest concentrations of Art Deco apartment buildings anywhere. It was cut through farmland years before the subway that would fill it arrived.

locations.name: The Lemon Ice King of Corona
locations.prompt: The Lemon Ice King of Corona
locations.factShort: Selling Italian ices on the same corner since 1944, in around thirty flavours, and famously refusing to put them in a cup with ice cream. The corner park outside appears in the opening credits of King of Queens.
